            (A) Section 4481(f). 
            (B) Section 4482(d).  
        (2) Extension and technical correction.—
            (A) In general.—Paragraph (4) of section 4482(c) of such Code is amended to read as follows:“(4) Taxable period.—The term ‘taxable period’ means any year beginning before July 1, 2017, and the period which begins on July 1, 2017, and ends at the close of September 30, 2017.”. 
            (B) Effective date.—The amendment made by this paragraph shall take effect as if included in the amendments made by section 142 of the Surface Transportation Extension Act of 2011, Part II.

        (2) by striking “December 31, 2012” each place it appears and inserting “March 31, 2017”, and 
        (3) by striking “October 1, 2012” and inserting “January 1, 2017”.

        (1) Section 4221(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking “July 1, 2012” and inserting “October 1, 2016”.

    (f) Effective Date.—Except as otherwise provided in this section, the amendments made by this section shall take effect on July 1, 2012.

fable.w: This section only extends expiration dates for highway-related excise taxes, exemptions, floor stocks refunds, and trust fund transfers by amending dates in the Internal Revenue Code. A tempting reading might treat the tax "refunds" or fund "transfers" as involving outside parties, but these are not consultation, comment, hearing, advisory, rulemaking, or right-to-sue provisions. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only extends dates in excise-tax, trust-fund-transfer and exemption provisions of the Internal Revenue Code and the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act. It requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue that would involve anyone outside the federal government. The 'floor stocks refunds' amendment only changes dates and is like a benefit claim, not participation in a federal decision.
opus.b: The tempting-but-wrong reading: "Floor Stocks Refunds" could look like an outside party making a claim to the government. That fails because a refund claim is like applying for a benefit, which the definition excludes. In any case, this section only changes dates. It sets up no process and involves no outside parties.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Internal Revenue Code, specifically extending expiration dates for various taxes and exemptions. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before these changes are made. The decision to extend these dates is made by Congress through legislation, not through a participatory process involving non-federal actors.
qwen_chat.s: (a) In General.— (1) Each of the following provisions of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking “June 30, 2012” and inserting “September 30, 2016”:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that extending tax provisions affects the public (taxpayers) and thus involves them. However, the definition of participation requires the government to *consult* or *coordinate* with outside parties *before* making a decision. This section simply amends dates in the tax code; it does not establish a process for public comment, hearings, or advisory input regarding those dates. The actors involved are Congress (amending the law) and the IRS (enforcing it), both inside the government.
